title: Pressure Direction
shortDefinition: Effective pressure has a specific direction: diagonal, to far hip, to shoulder line, or down through hip line.
whyItMatters: Straight-down pressure often lets opponents frame or hip escape; diagonal pressure makes them lose direction.
deepExplanation: Pressure Direction links head, sternum, pelvis, knees, and toes. When they do not point together, you feel heavy but do not control.
beginnerView: Ask where your force is going.
advancedView: Change Pressure Direction to make frames point the wrong way, then pass or pin.
